findings.reason: The original standalone image contains no figure. A based-loop schematic materially clarifies the ordered tree path / positive off-tree edge / reverse tree path correspondence central to [L2] and steps 1.1–2.1, even though the proof is independent.
findings.action: Added a fenced TikZ based-loop schematic and exact direction/path conventions in final Remarks.

correction: Added only final Remarks with a schematic H→Ht→Htx→H, dashed entire tree paths labeled t and overline(tx) inverse, and a solid positive x-edge outside T. Explained overlap/coincidence and inverse-loop conventions.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Vertices H, Ht, Htx in the right-coset Schreier graph; T is the given rooted spanning tree.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Statement, [L1], and def-schreier-generator identify these objects. This is a schematic of paths, not an asserted finite graph or embedded cycle; caption allows coincident vertices and overlapping tree paths.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Dashed outward path H→Ht reads t; dashed return Htx→H reads overline(tx)^{-1}.
diagram_math_checks.justification: [L2] and lem-spanning-trees-and-schreier-systems-correspond step 1.1 give unique root paths labeled by their representatives. Reversing the latter reverses order and inverts letters.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Solid positive edge e has source Ht, target Htx and label x∈X; for the displayed nontrivial generator e is outside T.
diagram_math_checks.justification: [L2] gives the source/target convention. The off-tree conclusion in item step 1.1 is valid: traversing any tree edge between the endpoints makes the based tree loop reduce to empty, including when that edge points toward the root.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Following arrows reads t x overline(tx)^{-1}=s(t,x); reversal reads s(t,x)^{-1} and traverses e backward.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Exact generator definition in def-schreier-generator and item [L2]; generators are indexed by x∈X only, so the backwards traversal is an inverse letter rather than a second positive-edge generator.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Three rendered vertex labels and three directed segments are present, including explicit Htx→H closing segment.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Independently viewed both native PNG tiles at original resolution; first tile contains the full diagram and all three arrowheads. No native --cycle closure is used.

preview.visual_result: All three directed paths and labels render without overlap or clipping; positive edge is left-to-right and closing dashed path points to H.
limitations: Native local ItemBody preview, not production route. Reference-title map records 16 unrelated parse diagnostics.

remaining_issues: Inherited proof 1.1 wording assumes a positive tree edge points away from the root: root→Ht followed by the edge may backtrack when the edge points toward the root. For H={1}, t=a^{-1}, x=a this occurs. The conclusion s(t,x)=1 remains valid after free reduction. Reported to coordinator; original proof preserved under assigned diagram-only scope.
